entries.title: DRAFT: sharp straight-path support threshold in lattice FPP
entries.statement: UNREVIEWED author-derived special case. In nearest-neighbor undirected FPP on Z^d, d>=2, with every edge weight in [a,b], 0<a<b, and integer n>=1, n(b-a)<=2a implies that T(0,n e1) equals the sum on the straight n-edge path. For iid laws with essential support endpoints a,b, n(b-a)>2a gives positive probability that an edge-disjoint (n+2)-edge dogleg beats that path. This is a finite-distance threshold, not an asymptotic exponent.
assumptions: iid with essential endpoints only for positive-probability sharpness

entries.title: DRAFT: exact variance in the continuous small-noise FPP window
entries.statement: UNREVIEWED author-derived special case. For iid Uniform[1,1+epsilon] edge weights on nearest-neighbor undirected Z^d, d>=2, epsilon>0, integer n>=1 and n epsilon<=2, T(0,n e1) is the straight-path sum, E T=n(1+epsilon/2), and Var T=n epsilon^2/12. These identities use independent weights on a deterministic path. They do not identify an exponent for a fixed law as n tends to infinity.

entries.title: DRAFT: necessary constant/onset tradeoff in normalized FPP variance bounds
entries.statement: UNREVIEWED author-derived necessary condition. For iid Uniform[1,1+epsilon] FPP on nearest-neighbor undirected Z^d, d>=2, 0<epsilon<=1, theta<1, K=floor(2/epsilon), suppose C>0 and integer N>=1 give Var T(0,n e1)<=C Var(tau_e) n^theta for every integer n>=N. Then either N>K or C>=K^(1-theta). Consequently no finite common C,N works over all epsilon for theta<1. This refutes only the law-uniform auxiliary bound; the per-fixed-law KPZ question is unaffected. No such asymptotic upper bound is proved here.
assumptions: The stated upper bound is a hypothesis; C,N may depend on epsilon in the necessary condition

relations.rationale: The threshold entry gives the straight-path identity under n(b-a)<=2a; with a=1,b=1+epsilon this is exactly the variance entry condition n epsilon<=2.
The variance entry states Var T=n epsilon^2/12. At K=floor(2/epsilon), division by Var(tau)=epsilon^2/12 gives C>=K^(1-theta) whenever N<=K.

The existing P0104 concept asks to "prove a fluctuation exponent strictly below1/2" under "suitable nondegenerate iid passage-time assumptions". This boundary entry explicitly restricts its obstruction to a "law-uniform auxiliary bound" and leaves the fixed-law parent unaffected. It documents a quantifier hazard, not a refutation of P0104.
